Rule: Prioritise works whose real-world documentation is scattered or missing; mainstream, already well-documented works rank last but are not excluded.
Why: Kyle, 2026-11-28: the archive aims to be comprehensive eventually, but its value now is centralising what the world has not (the site's thesis). Mainstream US/JP TV is hidden by default; Canadian/UK commercial TV is not hidden, just ranked last.
Example: Bulgarian and East German studio shorts before Nelvana series.

Rule: Select values (Country, Format, Technique, Genre, Keywords, platform, region) must come from the live Notion schema.
Why: Sessions 186–188 invented 7 stray options that had to be cleaned out of the schema.
Example: 'Free (ad-supported)' instead of ADS.

Rule: IMDb IDs only via Wikidata P345, else TMDB with a matching title; otherwise N/A.
Why: TMDB mis-maps some IDs; IMDb blocks fetches.
Example: Ghostbusters tt0127569 confirmed via Wikidata after a TMDB mis-map.

Rule: Duplicate check: an exact title, or a near title by the same director, counts up to ±5 years; read the year from any parenthetical in the Queue title.
Why: Production and release years differ; titles carry years in varied forms.
Example: Amazon Symphony (Queue 1951) = Sinfonia Amazônica (1953); 'Dogtanian (2021 CGI film)' read as having no year.

Rule: When several Queue items share a title, the draft names its item by queueId.
Why: Matching by title alone blocked Perlimps, which had two Queue items.
Example: Perlimps: April New item validated, February item marked Duplicate.

Rule: New directors need a sourced Nationality and new studios a Country and Type; otherwise the person or studio stays in the text only.
Why: A director without Nationality passed lint, Notion rejected it, and promote crashed mid-run.
Example: Kelly Dillon (Belly Flop) credited in text only.

Rule: Page icons must be a single standard emoji.
Why: Notion rejects non-emoji symbols and some newer joined emoji.
Example: ♜ (The Rook) and 🐦‍⬛ (Black Bird) rejected.

Rule: Treat Queue notes as leads, not facts; verify every field and record each overturned fact in conflicts and Notes.
Why: Across Sessions 190–195 about half of the April 2026 discovery items had a wrong studio, year, director or an invented theme.
Example: Zendegi was a Ministry of Culture film, not Kanoon; Kandittund! is 2021, not 2024.

Rule: A Queue 'Director' value may be a studio; find the credited director.
Why: Several Queue items listed studios as directors.
Example: Triggerfish (Troll Girl → Kay Carmichael), Lion Forge (Iyanu).

Rule: 'First / only / biggest' claims need native-language corroboration; otherwise attribute them to their source instead of stating them.
Why: Several Queue superlatives were false or narrower than claimed.
Example: The Last Fiction was not Iran's first animated feature (Tehran 1500, 2013); Piconzé was the second colour feature, not the first.

Rule: Each non-English work needs at least 2 native-language sources beyond Wikipedia filmographies, searched in the original script.
Why: Session 190 batch 2 leaned on English aggregators; a Persian pass then overturned years, titles and award claims.
Example: Bahador re-dated to 2000 from Kanoon News, YJC and Istanama.
Enforced By: review.mjs: native-source count; brief.mjs per-country lists

Rule: No watch link for foreign works that were still under copyright at home on 1 Jan 1996: their US copyright was restored (URAA).
Why: An Internet Archive upload of a 1938 Brazilian film was not public domain in the US.
Example: Macaco Feio, Macaco Bonito: protected in Brazil to 2008, so US copyright runs to 2033.

Rule: Watch links only from official channels, verified streaming title pages or genuine public-domain archives.
Why: Unofficial re-uploads disappear and misrepresent rights.
Example: Triggerfish's own YouTube for Troll Girl; no Aparat re-uploads of Kanoon films.

Rule: Institutional and distributor copy inflates award names; cross-check prizes against festival records.
Why: Persian press repeated Kanoon's 'Golden Palm' for a Cannes Junior prize.
Example: Bahador: Cannes Junior Grand Prix 2001, not a Palme d'Or.

Rule: Private archives, fan wikis and lifestyle portals are supporting evidence only.
Why: parand.se copied runtimes between pages; Namuwiki and Lost Media wikis are unvetted.
Example: parand.se rated Low in the Sources DB.

Rule: Record production year and release year when they differ; Year holds the first public release or premiere.
Why: Many Queue years were production or announcement years.
Example: Kiya: 2015 Story Lab selection vs 2023 premiere.

Rule: Country follows creative origin (where a work was conceived and creatively led), not the lead financier; explain the choice in Notes.
Why: Lead-producer rules pushed African works into USA/France, where K1 would hide them, against the site's thesis.
Example: Iwájú = Nigeria; Supa Team 4 = Zambia; Kiya = South Africa; Iyanu = Nigeria; Klincus = Italy; Bernard = South Korea; Moein's TED-Ed lessons = Iran.

Rule: One Films entry per series; later seasons are Queue Duplicates, with a dated note on the series entry.
Why: Season-level entries fragment the catalogue.
Example: Supa Team 4 covers seasons 1–2; Brave Animated Series 2 → Duplicate of the 2021 entry.

Rule: Sequels and spin-offs are linked through a Series & Universes entry with the original.
Why: Keeps franchises navigable.
Example: Willy Fog, David the Gnome, Dogtanian, Ejen Ali, Chhota Bheem, Monica and Friends series.

Rule: Live-action/CGI hybrids qualify, with Technique Mixed and an honest note on the animation's share.
Why: The archive already held hybrids.
Example: ReBoot: The Guardian Code, Saving Sally, Mikolo.

Rule: Thinly documented lost early films: Confidence ★★ and the director marked '(attributed)'.
Why: Keeps historically important lost works without overstating certainty.
Example: On a Moonlit Night (1934) → Jambu Kaka (1934).

Rule: A work that cannot be verified after three research levels goes to Queue status Cannot Find, with the search log in Notes.
Why: Conflated Queue entries should not be invented into records.
Example: Dunia Dekou; Kahwa (Session 192).

Rule: Emigré directors take the nationality of the country where they made their work.
Why: Consistency with existing pages.
Example: Norman McLaren = Canada; Ypê Nakashima = Brazil.

Rule: When BRB series credits dispute the screen director, link creator Claudio Biern Boyd and state the dispute in Notes.
Why: Neither disputed name had enough sourcing for a page; matches The World of David the Gnome.
Example: Willy Fog 2; The Return of Dogtanian.

Rule: Wikidata often files socialist-era works under the predecessor state; discovery includes a predecessor only when this country alone replaced it.
Why: Bulgarian works point at the People's Republic of Bulgaria; East Germany's shared predecessor pulled in pre-1945 German films.
Example: Bulgaria 8 → 92 candidates; East Germany 116 → 67 after the fix.

Rule: Never override human curation (Unavailable, a dated Verified, or Kyle's edits); snapshot before writes and log every write.
Why: The first cron run overwrote 586 curated link statuses, which were then restored from a snapshot.
Example: platform-trust.js reconcileStatus.

Rule: Session numbers are strictly sequential, and Session 46 import items are excluded until re-sourced in Chinese.
Why: Validation Protocol numbering lesson; Session 46 import flagged unreliable.
Example: log-session.mjs refuses a reused number.

Rule: Add good sources found in research to the Sources DB after review, and flag sources that proved wrong.
Why: The Sources DB was not used or fed until Session 195.
Example: 13 sources added from Sessions 190–195 (Filmografia Brasileira, Sourehcinema…).
